rules.message: Prisma $queryRaw or $executeRaw with template literal interpolation
rules.detail: Using $queryRaw or $executeRaw with template literal expressions that include user input bypasses Prisma's SQL injection protection. Use the tagged template literal form $queryRaw`SELECT ... WHERE id = ${id}` which auto-parameterises, or pass a Prisma.sql`` tagged template.

rules.message: Prisma findMany() without a where clause — potential data exposure
rules.detail: Calling findMany() without a where clause returns all records. In a multi-tenant application this can expose data belonging to other users. Always filter by the authenticated user's ID or tenant ID.

rules.message: Prisma include or select built from user-controlled input
rules.detail: Allowing users to control which relations are included in a query can expose sensitive related data or enable denial-of-service via deeply nested includes. Whitelist permitted fields.

rules.message: Prisma deleteMany() without where clause — mass deletion risk
rules.detail: Calling deleteMany() without a where clause deletes every record in the table. Always provide a specific where clause to limit scope.

rules.message: Prisma updateMany() without where clause — mass update risk
rules.detail: Calling updateMany() without a where clause updates every record. Always provide a specific where clause.

rules.message: Prisma create() with unvalidated request body spread
rules.detail: Spreading the entire request body into a Prisma create() call allows attackers to set fields they shouldn't (e.g. isAdmin, role, balance). Explicitly list permitted fields.

cves.description: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Attributes
